title: kwave-power-law-attenuation-calibration: Reproducible numerical audit of k-Wave power-law attenuation calibration and sensitivity near y=1
description:
kwave-power-law-attenuation-calibration provides a reproducible numerical audit of power-law acoustic attenuation in k-Wave simulations (under MATLAB and CUDA), focusing on two independent sources of error: literature parameter transfer and the numerical dispersion singularity near y = 1.

Key Audit Findings

  • Parameter Conversion Bias (y = 2): Directly using a literature linear attenuation coefficient (y = 1) in k-Wave's default quadratic model (y = 2) biases attenuation away from the reference frequency (by −50.13% at 0.5 MHz). Applying the derived analytical matching formula eliminates this bias (reducing error to −0.97%).
  • Near-y = 1 Dispersion Deficit: Operating near y = 1 with k-Wave's default dispersion mode silently induces large attenuation errors due to the singular Kramers-Kronig dispersion relation. At y = 1.01, the solver exhibits a −56.8% to −59.4% multiplicative attenuation deficit across 0.2–1.0 MHz (R² ≥ 0.999), and an independent 3-D control exhibits a matching +57% excess in peak pressure. Switching to no_dispersion resolves this deficit.
  • Field Divergence & Collapse: Approaching y = 1 closer (y = 0.99) causes numerical failure: the 1-D peak pressure collapses into residual noise, while the 3-D field diverges to order 1030 Pa across both MATLAB and CUDA backends.

Repository Contents

  • Core Experiments: Controlled 1-D k-Wave simulation scripts and 3-D backend verification controls.
  • Reproducibility: Pre-computed raw JSON metrics for all exponent sweeps, allowing instant figure reproduction without a MATLAB license.
  • Full Technical Report: 16-page technical report with full LaTeX source (report.tex) and compiled PDF.

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/Yuewang04/kwave-power-law-attenuation-calibration
